quandoUsar: The scroll area of a conversation that receives new messages or streaming text and should follow the end while the reader is there.
When scrolling up should release the follow behavior, without pulling the reader back, and offer a shortcut to the latest message.
Live logs in general (run logs, event feeds) where new content enters from the bottom.
quandoEvitar: Use `scroll-area` for static content that only needs thin scrollbars and edge fades.
Use `chat-thread` or `chat-app` when you want the ready-made conversation, with messages and input field, and not just the container.
Use `infinite-masonry` for feeds that load more items on reaching the end, instead of following what arrives.

teclado.acao: With focus on the area, scroll the conversation (native scrolling) and immediately interrupt the automatic slide to the end.
Moves focus to the scroll area, which is focusable, then to whatever is interactive in the messages and to the jump button.
On the “Jump to latest” button, returns to the end; focus moves to the scroll area, because the button disappears.

acessibilidade: The visible area is a focusable `role="region"` named by `label`; the content is a `role="log"` with `aria-live="polite"`, so new messages are announced.
The jump button shows the text of `jumpLabel`, and the counter has an `aria-label` with the number of new messages (in English, with no translation prop).
When the button is activated by keyboard, focus goes to the scroll area instead of being lost when the button leaves.
movimento: New messages rise with a spring and a slight scale-up; those already present on the first render do not animate.
The return to the end is a spring slide in the scroll position; the jump button emerges from below and the unread number rolls to each new total.
With “reduce motion” on, scrolling goes straight to the end, and messages and button only fade.
responsivo: The height comes from `--message-scroller-height` (default 22rem) or from `className` and `style`; scrolling is internal, and the top and bottom edges fade when there is more content in that direction.
desempenho: Two `ResizeObserver`s track the content and the frame; there is no virtualization and each child gets an animated wrapper, so limit the history in very long conversations.
notasIA: Each direct child counts as one message: give each a stable `key`; the unread counter compares the number of children, so trimming old messages while new ones arrive makes it stop going up.

Set the height (variable `--message-scroller-height`, `className` or `style`); `onAtBottomChange` signals when the reader leaves the end or returns, and `threshold` (32 px) says what still counts as the end.
It pairs with `message-bubble` or `message` as children; pass `animateIn={false}` to them, because the animated entrance is already handled here (`animateItems`).
